title: Putin announces partial mobilisation of Russian reservists
body:
On 21 September 2022, Russian President Vladimir Putin announced a partial mobilisation in a televised address and signed a decree to begin it immediately. The measure stopped short of a full draft. Putin said that only citizens currently in the reserve would be called up, with priority for those who had served in the army or had relevant professions and experience.

Defence Minister Sergei Shoigu said 300,000 reservists would be called up to hold the line at the front. He also said 5,937 Russian soldiers had died in Ukraine, a figure far below Western estimates. The announcement came a day after Russian-controlled areas of Ukraine announced referendums on joining Russia, and followed Ukrainian advances in the Kharkiv counteroffensive.

In his speech Putin accused the collective West of trying to weaken and destroy Russia. He said Russia would use all available means to defend itself and its people, and noted that Russia has a nuclear arsenal. He said Russia had a moral obligation to protect civilians in the occupied areas holding referendums. US Ambassador to Ukraine Bridget Brink described the move as a sign of weakness and failure and said the United States would never recognise any claimed annexation. Putin announced on 28 October 2022 that the mobilisation had been completed.
